programme: NCOA1 acting as a p160/SRC-family steroid- and nuclear-receptor coactivator: recruited by estrogen receptor/LXR in sensory tissue to shape nociceptive gene programmes, and, separately, a recurrent MEIS1::NCOA1 gene-fusion partner whose coactivator domain is repurposed to drive an oncogenic transcriptional programme in specific sarcoma subtypes.
role_in_a: In fibromyalgia-relevant sensory tissue, NCOA1 coactivates LXR/estrogen-receptor signaling, and this axis represses pronociceptive effects of estrogen — i.e. normal NCOA1-dependent coactivation dampens pain sensitization, consistent with fibromyalgia's hormonally-modulated, female-predominant pain phenotype.
role_in_b: In sarcoma, NCOA1 is a recurrent fusion partner (MEIS1::NCOA1) that creates a chimeric transcription factor retaining NCOA1's coactivator domain, driving distinct primitive spindle-cell/pelvic sarcoma entities through aberrant activation of MEIS1 target genes in mesenchymal cells.
shared_axis: Both diseases converge on the same molecular part — NCOA1's coactivator domain — but use it for unrelated ends: physiological modulation of nociceptive signaling in one, oncogenic transcriptional hijacking via chromosomal fusion in the other. This is a shared building block, not a shared disease mechanism.
reasoning: NCOA1 is the only factor in the list independently and specifically placed in both diseases by retrieved papers, which sets it apart from the rest of the list (largely sarcoma-only or entirely unsupported). But its two documented roles — coactivator of estrogen/LXR signaling in pain modulation versus a fusion oncoprotein in mesenchymal sarcoma — are mechanistically distinct, and nothing retrieved ties fibromyalgia and sarcoma together through it; the connection is my synthesis of a shared molecular component, not a documented disease-disease link.
support: PMID 38590761 shows NCOA1-dependent LXR/estrogen-receptor coactivation represses pronociceptive signaling, placing it in a fibromyalgia-relevant pain-modulation context. PMID 40420135 and PMID 40160183 each report recurrent MEIS1::NCOA1 fusions defining distinct primitive spindle-cell sarcoma entities (pelvic and renal), placing NCOA1 as a structural oncogenic driver in sarcoma. PMID 42449878 reports a related MEIS1::NCOA2 fusion sarcoma, supporting the same fusion mechanism in the NCOA paralog family but not NCOA1 itself.
how_to_falsify: In a nociceptor/DRG model, knock down NCOA1 and test whether estrogen/LXR-dependent modulation of muscle pressure hyperalgesia is lost — if pain thresholds are unaffected, the fibromyalgia-side mechanism fails. Separately, screen fibromyalgia patient blood/muscle samples for MEIS1::NCOA1 fusion transcripts (expected absent) and for altered wild-type NCOA1 target-gene activity (ESR1/ESR2/NR3C1) versus controls — if there is no differential NCOA1-pathway activity in fibromyalgia cases, the account has nothing to stand on.
caveats: Only 3 independent cohort pairs underlie the 40 patient-group comparisons, and NCOA1 itself is concordant in just 20/40 (50%), a modest majority rather than a strong signal. The tissue pairing (blood for fibromyalgia vs. soft tissue for sarcoma) is anatomically disconnected, which is why the account rests on shared molecular machinery rather than shared physiology. Ten of the twelve listed factors (MYF6, ATF4, HCFC1, ARID4A, CBFA2T3, KLF15, GSX1, NKRF, DMRT1, TFDP3, ATF5) have no credible fibromyalgia evidence and are largely sarcoma-only or unconfirmed even there, so this account deliberately does not use most of the list. Tissue-generic exclusions (RUNX2, MEF2C, STAT1, IKZF1, etc.) removed an easier myogenic/immune story before ranking — their absence is by design, not oversight — and the single-view exclusions (RERE, MAZ, IRF5, etc.) rule out a narrative built on one patient subgroup.
